answer.rationale: Negotiating terms with the incumbent leverages our stable integration (memory_c1: 'no migration work and no interruption') and has direct precedent for cost recovery via benchmarking (memory_c4: 'recovered real margin... moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms'). This action directly targets the 18% spend cut mandate without introducing the delivery risk inherent in switching vendors (time-pressured onboarding at 94% capacity) or the uncertainty of deferral (contract expires in 14 days). While negotiation carries risk of supplier pushback, it is lower than the operational risk of switching (memory_c2's success required 'quick onboarding'—unreliable under current constraints) or the cost uncertainty of second-sourcing (memory_c3 addresses risk, not cost).
